VIDEO.title: The Hidden Meaning Behind Jesus' Silence
VIDEO.series: The Gospel of Matthew Every Word (playlist of 58 videos)

kicker: Study aid · Matthew 26:47-75 · Episode 53 (#56 of 58 in the playlist)
hand: He did not open His mouth
SUMMARY: The teacher reads Matthew 26:47-75. Judas arrives with a large crowd from the chief priests and elders and kisses Jesus: 'Greetings, Rabbi!' One of the disciples cuts off the ear of the high priest's slave; Jesus tells him to put his sword away, says He could appeal for more than twelve legions of angels, and that the Scriptures must be fulfilled. The disciples flee. Before Caiaphas, false witnesses fail until two speak of destroying the sanctuary. Jesus keeps silent until put under oath, then speaks of the Son of Man at the right hand of Power. He is condemned for blasphemy, spat on and struck. In the courtyard Peter denies Him three times, the rooster crows, and Peter weeps bitterly.

The arresting party likely included temple police and Roman soldiers (John 18:3, 12); John names the swordsman as Peter and the slave as Malchus (John 18:10), and Luke records the healing (Luke 22:51). 'Robber' (lēstēs) can mean rebel. The council named is the chief priests, scribes and elders, not the Pharisees: the video reads this as a plot led by a corrupt priestly circle, meeting at night in a house.

Two witnesses were needed (Deuteronomy 17:6; 19:15). Jesus' silence fulfills Isaiah 53:7. 'Christ' and 'Son of God' go together (2 Samuel 7:14; Psalm 2:7), and Jesus joins Daniel 7:13-14 with Psalm 110:1. Blasphemy carried death (Leviticus 24:16). Peter's denial means disowning, and it may have happened while Jesus was confessing inside.
Connections: the kiss and the friend (Proverbs 27:6; Psalm 55:12-13; 41:9); Jesus' word about the sword and Jeremiah 15:2; the spitting and striking (Isaiah 50:6-7).

The lesson: Jesus prayed before His suffering, but once it began He did not ask to end it. Because suffering is appointed by God, we must not rush to end it without allowing its purpose to be fulfilled.
QUOTES: Because suffering is appointed by God, we must not rush to end it without allowing its purpose to be fulfilled.
Jesus knows the scripture so well that he fulfills it in the face of false accusations.
Jesus prayed to the Father to alleviate his suffering before it took place, but once it started, he never asked to alleviate it again.
The testimony of the Christian suffering is a shout of praise to the God of heaven.

method.p: Read the same passage each day for five days; the video's insight about Jesus not praying at His arrest came only after several readings.

LSB_QUOTES.text: Or do you think that I cannot appeal to My Father, and He will at once put at My disposal more than twelve legions of angels?
He was oppressed and He was afflicted, / Yet He did not open His mouth; / Like a lamb that is led to slaughter, / And like a sheep that is silent before its shearers, / So He did not open His mouth.
And the Lord turned and looked at Peter.

left.text: And immediately Judas went to Jesus and said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed Him. And Jesus said to him, “Friend, do what you have come for.” Then they came and laid hands on Jesus and seized Him.

right.text: Faithful are the wounds of a friend, / But deceitful are the kisses of an enemy.

lines.text: The crowd wanted Jesus alone; in a dark grove it would be hard to tell Him from His students, so Judas offers a sign of respect and friendship. Jesus asks, 'Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?' (Luke 22:48).
David's lament fits: 'it is you, a man my equal, / My close companion and my familiar friend' (Psalm 55:13), along with Psalm 41:9.

The party probably included the chief priests and elders (Luke 22:52), temple police and Roman soldiers (John 18:3, 12). Pilate may have known from the start, which could explain his wife's dream (27:19).

left.text: Simon Peter then, having a sword, drew it and struck the high priest’s slave, and cut off his right ear; and the slave’s name was Malchus.

right.text: But Jesus answered and said, “Stop! No more of this.” And He touched his ear and healed him.

lines.text: Peter's violence should have got him arrested with Jesus; perhaps the public rebuke kept him safe. 'All those who take up the sword shall perish by the sword' recalls Jeremiah 15:2.
'Robber' (lēstēs) can also mean rebel: they come as if against an armed rebellion, though He sat in the temple every day. The question has a note of sarcasm.
'The Scriptures of the prophets' are not named; they point to the suffering servant (Psalm 22; Isaiah 50:6; 52:13-53:12; Daniel 9:26; Zechariah 12:10; Micah 5:1).

left.text: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin kept trying to obtain false testimony against Jesus, so that they might put Him to death. And they did not find any, even though many false witnesses came forward. But later on two came forward,

right.text: On the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses, he who is to die shall be put to death; he shall not be put to death on the mouth of one witness.

lines.text: The council named is Caiaphas, the chief priests, scribes and elders, not the Pharisees. The video reads this as a plot led by a corrupt priestly circle tied to the temple trade and to Rome, which acted within a week of Jesus confronting them.

Many believe the full Sanhedrin did not sit: it was night, not day, and in a house, not the temple. The Mishnah says of capital cases: 'the court judges during the daytime, and concludes the deliberations and issues the ruling only in the daytime' (Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:1).

src.text: And the high priest stood up and said to Him, “Do You not answer? What are these men testifying against You?” But Jesus kept silent. And the high priest said to Him, “I put You under oath by the living God, that You tell us whether You are the Christ, the Son of God.”

lines.text: Jesus does not defend Himself against the misleading charge. He fulfills Isaiah 53:7, where the servant 'did not open His mouth.' Anyone else would defend their character; He let the Scripture guide His actions.
He speaks only when asked whether He is the Messiah. The video leaves you a question: why silence on the one issue and not the other?

TRIAL.title: At the right hand of Power

left.text: “I kept looking in the night visions, / And behold, with the clouds of heaven / One like a Son of Man was coming, / And He came up to the Ancient of Days / And came near before Him.

right.text: Yahweh says to my Lord: / “Sit at My right hand / Until I put Your enemies as a footstool for Your feet.”

lines.text: 'Christ' and 'Son of God' go together because of 2 Samuel 7:14, Psalm 2:7 and Psalm 89:26-27: 'You are My Son, / Today I have begotten You.'

Blasphemy carried death (Leviticus 24:16). The Mishnah says the blasphemer 'is not liable unless he utters the name of God' (Mishnah Sanhedrin 7:5), which Jesus did not do; the charge must be that He made Himself God, as in John 10:33.

src.text: Then he began to curse and swear, “I do not know the man!” And immediately a rooster crowed. And Peter remembered the word which Jesus had said, “Before a rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.” And he went out and cried bitterly.

lines.text: The word for deny also means disown. While Jesus affirms His identity inside and is condemned, Peter in the courtyard calls a curse on himself to disown Him. Then 'the Lord turned and looked at Peter' (Luke 22:61).

DENIAL.title: I did not hide My face

left.text: Then they spat in His face and beat Him with their fists; and others slapped Him, and said, “Prophesy to us, O Christ; who is the one who hit You?”

right.text: I gave My back to those who strike Me, / And My cheeks to those who pluck out the beard; / I did not hide My face from dishonor and spitting. / Even now Lord Yahweh helps Me, / Therefore, I am not dishonored; / Therefore, I have set My face like flint, / And I know that I will not be ashamed.

lines.text: Two kinds of people fulfill Scripture here: Caiaphas and the leaders, for their own ends, and Jesus, who fulfills it properly (5:17). Even the unnamed men who spat on Him fulfill Isaiah 50.

BACKGROUND.p: Caiaphas held office c. AD 18-36. An ossuary inscribed 'Joseph son of Caiaphas' was found in Jerusalem in 1990. Large priestly houses had courtyards where servants and guards could gather by a fire (Luke 22:55).
Later rabbinic rules (Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:1) required capital cases to be tried and concluded by day. Whether these rules were in force in Jesus' day is debated.
'The way you talk gives you away' (26:73): Galileans had a recognizable regional accent.

WITNESSES.text: And not even when reminded of his sin by Christ did he dare to weep openly, lest he should be betrayed by his tears, but he went out, and wept bitterly.

DEBATES.h: A formal trial or a hearing?
DEBATES.p: Some see a full night session of the Sanhedrin; others an informal hearing at Caiaphas' house, followed by a morning meeting (27:1).
The video leaves this as a question. Many answer that Jesus would not defend Himself against false charges but would not deny who He is.
The Mishnah's narrow rule required the divine name. Most think the charge was Jesus' claim to share God's throne (Daniel 7; Psalm 110).

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: Matthew does not name the Pharisees at the trial, but they join the chief priests before Pilate in 27:62.
The Mishnah's trial rules were written down around AD 200; whether they bound the court in Jesus' day is debated.
The link between the priests and the temple trade is a reconstruction; Matthew does not spell it out.
Psalm 55:12-13 spans two verses in the LSB.

QUESTIONS: Why do you think Jesus called Judas 'Friend'?
What does Jesus' rebuke of Peter's sword teach about His kingdom?
Why did Jesus keep silent on the false charge but answer about being the Christ?
How do Daniel 7 and Psalm 110 shape Jesus' answer to Caiaphas?
Peter disowned Jesus while Jesus confessed Himself. Where are you tempted to disown Him?
What suffering in your life might have a purpose you have not yet seen?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: The lesson: Jesus prayed before His suffering began, but once it started He never asked to end it, because the Father wills it. Because suffering is appointed by God, we must not rush to end it without allowing its purpose to be fulfilled (Deuteronomy 32; 1 Samuel 2; Ecclesiastes 3; Isaiah 45; John 9:3). The teacher shares that his father was paralyzed in a 2009 accident and was never healed; yet through it he, his wife and children came to faith, the ministry began, and his parents have witnessed to many. He has learned to pray not for suffering to end at once but for strength to endure it.
APPLICATION_ADDED: Study note (added): read Matthew 26:47-75 once a day for five days this week, and on the last day write down one thing you noticed that you missed on the first.

- Judas: Signals with a kiss of respect and friendship. [Background] Jesus still calls him 'Friend' (26:50).
- Malchus: The high priest's slave whose right ear Peter cuts off. [Background] Named only in John 18:10; Luke records the healing.
- Caiaphas: The high priest who puts Jesus under oath and tears his garments. [Background] High priest c. AD 18-36, son-in-law of Annas (John 18:13).
- Peter: Draws the sword, follows at a distance, disowns Jesus three times. [Background] Restored later by the sea (John 21:15-17).
- Pilate's wife: Her dream may suggest Pilate knew of the arrest that night. [Background] Named only in later tradition.

## Places [Background]
- Gethsemane (traditional) (named in the video): Where Judas came with the crowd (26:47).
- Temple: 'Every day I used to sit in the temple teaching' (26:55).
- Court of Caiaphas (traditional) (named in the video): They 'led Him away to Caiaphas, the high priest' (26:57).

## Key terms
- Sanhedrin: The ruling council in Jerusalem, led by the high priest.
- Legion: A Roman unit of several thousand soldiers. [Background]
- Lēstēs: Robber, bandit; also an insurrectionist.
- Blasphemy: Speaking against God; under Leviticus 24:16 a capital offense.

- καταφιλέω kataphileō (G2705, Greek): To kiss, often warmly or repeatedly. (Matt 26:49)

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- The high priest's house: Caiaphas held office c. AD 18-36. An ossuary inscribed 'Joseph son of Caiaphas' was found in Jerusalem in 1990. Large priestly houses had courtyards where servants and guards could gather by a fire (Luke 22:55).
- Night trials: Later rabbinic rules (Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:1) required capital cases to be tried and concluded by day. Whether these rules were in force in Jesus' day is debated.
- Galilean speech: 'The way you talk gives you away' (26:73): Galileans had a recognizable regional accent.

## Early witnesses [Background: sourced]
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "And not even when reminded of his sin by Christ did he dare to weep openly, lest he should be betrayed by his tears, but he went out, and wept bitterly." Homilies on Matthew 85, on 26:75. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "Who was this one, who cut off the ear? John says that it was Peter." Homilies on Matthew 84, on 26:51. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- A formal trial or a hearing? Some see a full night session of the Sanhedrin; others an informal hearing at Caiaphas' house, followed by a morning meeting (27:1).
- Why silence, then speech? The video leaves this as a question. Many answer that Jesus would not defend Himself against false charges but would not deny who He is.
- What was the blasphemy? The Mishnah's narrow rule required the divine name. Most think the charge was Jesus' claim to share God's throne (Daniel 7; Psalm 110).

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- Matthew does not name the Pharisees at the trial, but they join the chief priests before Pilate in 27:62.
- The Mishnah's trial rules were written down around AD 200; whether they bound the court in Jesus' day is debated.
- The link between the priests and the temple trade is a reconstruction; Matthew does not spell it out.
- Psalm 55:12-13 spans two verses in the LSB.

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. Why do you think Jesus called Judas 'Friend'?
2. What does Jesus' rebuke of Peter's sword teach about His kingdom?
3. Why did Jesus keep silent on the false charge but answer about being the Christ?
4. How do Daniel 7 and Psalm 110 shape Jesus' answer to Caiaphas?
5. Peter disowned Jesus while Jesus confessed Himself. Where are you tempted to disown Him?
6. What suffering in your life might have a purpose you have not yet seen?

## Application
- (video) The lesson: Jesus prayed before His suffering began, but once it started He never asked to end it, because the Father wills it. Because suffering is appointed by God, we must not rush to end it without allowing its purpose to be fulfilled (Deuteronomy 32; 1 Samuel 2; Ecclesiastes 3; Isaiah 45; John 9:3). The teacher shares that his father was paralyzed in a 2009 accident and was never healed; yet through it he, his wife and children came to faith, the ministry began, and his parents have witnessed to many. He has learned to pray not for suffering to end at once but for strength to endure it.
- Study note (added): read Matthew 26:47-75 once a day for five days this week, and on the last day write down one thing you noticed that you missed on the first.
